title: Guardrail regression and split-testing walkthrough - Rivermark
summary: Redwood AE/SE demo of Eval/Quality features: building prompt sets, configuring regression alerts tied to prompt sets, running A/B comparisons, and using the Console + Optimize recommendations. Customer focused on minimizing false positives in alerts, data residency, and pilot success criteria. Next steps: share security pack, sample eval CSV, pricing for 3-month pilot, and schedule bench test for latency/cost metrics.

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-01-16 15:30 UTC, Duration ~48m, Attendees listed above.

00:00 Maya (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick intro, I'm Maya, account executive at Redwood, and Oliver our solutions engineer will run the demo.
00:12 Tom (Product): Hey thanks. We're excited — trying to get a clearer picture of how Redwood's eval/quality features would fit into our customer chat pipeline.
00:20 Oliver (SE): Great. The goal for today is to show prompt sets, how you can monitor regression alerts, and run A/B comparisons across model variants and rollout percentages. We'll use a demo prompt set modeled on a financial summarization flow.
00:34 Anya (Head of ML): High level, we care about false positives from alerts — last vendor spammed us after every small nudge. Also data residency — some logs can't leave region.
00:45 Maya (AE): Noted. We'll show the Console settings for retention and private sychron-- sync? I mean private deployments and KMS for keys.
00:51 Priya (Security): Quick Q: SOC2? SSO/SAML? Can we map roles to RBAC controls?
01:00 Oliver (SE): Yes, SOC2 and RBAC, SSO via SAML/OIDC. The Console supports team roles and token scoping. For private we can hook into your KMS/HSM. We'll follow up with the whitepaper.
01:14 Oliver (SE): Ok walkthrough — opening Console -> Evalops -> Prompt Sets. (screen share noises).
01:28 Oliver: Here we created a prompt set called "transaction-summaries-v1" — it's a set of 120 prompts covering edge cases (missing fields, multi-currency, dispute language). You can tag prompts by intent and expected label.
01:45 Jason (Data Eng): Are annotations stored with customer data or are they stored by Redwood?
01:52 Oliver: Annotations can be stored in your VPC variant or in Redwood hosted encryption-at-rest — you choose retention policies per-org. The transcript may be slightly fuzzy there but we have a per-tenant toggle.
02:10 Oliver: Now the Eval dashboard; you can select a slice (e.g., high-value accounts), choose metrics like "BLEU-ish scores", but more typical for us is pairwise diff on custom metrics — for example, "accuracy of expense categorization" or "safety flag rate."
02:34 Tom: How are regression alerts configured? We don't want a flood but need sensitivity.
02:40 Oliver: Alerts are threshold-based and stats-aware. You can set a baseline window (14d) with statistical significance (p-value) and control for minimum sample size. There's also a "quiet window" to suppress noisy alerts during deploys.
02:55 Anya: Can we tie alerts to specific prompt IDs? We want to know which prompt triggered the regression.
03:02 Oliver: Yes — each prompt in a prompt set has an ID and the alert will show top contributing prompts and example diffs.
03:14 Maya (AE): We'll demo an A/B run now — routing 10% traffic to a quantized model and 90% to a standard model and show pairwise comparison.
03:25 Oliver: Spinning up an experiment: choose control and treatment, define traffic split, metric set, and evaluation window. The Console can auto-sample and produce an A/B compare report with statistical significance.
03:40 Priya: In terms of telemetry, what goes to Redwood? We need minimal PII and ability to redact.
03:48 Oliver: You can mask PII client-side or use Redwood's built-in scrubbers. For Private deployments logs can remain in your VPC; hosted still supports tokenization and field masks.
04:05 Tom: Cost question — those A/B sampling and eval runs add to bill?
04:10 Maya: Yes they're treated as eval jobs; Optimize will recommend batching/quant settings to minimize unit cost. We'll share an estimate for the pilot.
04:22 Oliver: Now I'm opening an historical regression alert — here's an alert for safety flag rate increase. See the top n prompts that shifted. There's also a link to the raw examples and an option to rerun locally in the sandbox.
04:45 Anya: That example looks like a false positive due to tokenization differences. Can we filter out prompts with <= 5 tokens?
04:52 Oliver: Yep — you can set filters in the prompt-set slice. You can also create derived metrics, e.g., ignore short prompts, or bucket by length.
05:05 Tom: If we want to run everything on-prem, does the console still work?
05:11 Oliver: We ship a Private control plane — Console can be deployed in your VPC and talk to the inference plane over private networking. There are some managed features that require a sync endpoint, but core evals and alerts run locally.
05:25 Priya: What about KMS integration and audit logs for compliance?
05:30 Oliver: Integrations with AWS KMS, Google KMS, HSMs, plus full audit logs per-route, per-token. We'll include the diagrams in the security pack.
05:44 Maya (AE): Quick demo of Optimize suggestions — it scans your traffic distribution, suggests quantization profiles and batching targets, and shows estimated cost delta vs quality.
06:00 Oliver: For example, it suggests int8 quant for the summarization model with a 0.8% quality drop but 40% cost savings on token spend for this workload.
06:15 Anya: We'll be conservative — quality drop needs to be under 0.2% for certain SLAs.
06:21 Oliver: Understood. You can pin baseline thresholds and Optimize will only recommend within those constraints.
06:30 Tom: Walk me through a full pilot flow — how do we measure success after 30 days?
06:36 Maya: Typical pilot: 3 model variants, 3 prompt sets, evaluate daily sampling, regression alerts on primary metrics, and monthly rollups. Success criteria: no critical functional regressions, latency within 250ms p95 for web route, and under targeted cost per 1k tokens.
06:52 Jason: What's the onboarding time for a pilot?
06:56 Diego (Solutions): Usually 2 weeks for sandbox + config, 1 week for pilot ramp, so ~3-4 weeks end-to-end if infra's ready.
07:08 Priya: Any known limitations?
07:10 Oliver: Some very high-frequency telemetry (millions of individual prompt traces) we recommend sampled ingest to keep costs down; also extremely long sequences can affect metric similarity.
07:22 Anya: Can we attach our own evaluators? Like run our internal rubric and push scores?
07:28 Oliver: Yes. You can push external eval CSVs mapped to prompt IDs — Console will merge and show pairwise comparisons.
07:35 Tom: Show the A/B compare report.
07:37 Oliver: (navigates) Here's the compare: metric table with lift, p-value, confidence intervals, and examples where treatment changed the label. You can click into failing prompts and create a ticket or rollback the rollout.
07:58 Tom: Nice. Do you have programmatic API for these reports?
08:03 Oliver: Absolutely — API endpoints to create experiments, fetch metrics, and pull example diffs. We also stream events to your event bus for infra automation.
08:15 Anya: We'll want to fetch example diffs and pipe into our annotation tool. How fast is that export?
08:21 Oliver: Exports are near real-time for small slices; larger historical exports are async with a callback webhook.
08:30 Priya: Security follow-up: Can devs be scoped so they can't see raw customer text?
08:36 Oliver: Yes, token-level RBAC and view-only roles; you can hide raw text and show only diffs or masked examples.
08:45 Maya (AE): Let's simulate a regression alert now. I'll toggle a synthetic drift on the treatment to raise the failure rate.
08:53 Oliver: Running a quick replay of a small sample... (typing) and there it is — alert generated: "Expense classification accuracy drop: control 92.3% -> treatment 89.1% (p<0.01)". The alert shows top 5 prompts and sample diffs.
09:18 Tom: That example would have triggered a manual rollback. Can we auto-fallback?
09:23 Oliver: Yes, Redwood supports auto-fallback policies — if metric breach is detected, traffic shifts back to a fallback variant and it can create an incident in your system.
09:34 Anya: For the pilot we need a playbook: what triggers alert, who owns it, and auto vs manual.
09:39 Maya: We'll draft a runbook template and attach to the pilot docs.
09:44 Tom: Any pricing ballpark for a 3-month pilot with 50k tokens/day and eval sampling?
09:49 Maya: I'll send a tailored pilot pricing. Roughly the hosted evaling and A/B tooling adds small percent above inference spend; we can also run on Dedicated if you prefer fixed monthly.
10:00 Jason: We have a question about token accounting — do eval tokens count toward bill?
10:05 Maya: Yes, eval samples and reruns count, but we show per-route breakdown in Console so you can attribute costs to pilots and production.
10:14 Tom: Ok. A couple of quick technicals — does the A/B run preserve KV cache state? We rely on long-context KV caching for chat.
10:22 Oliver: Good point. For chat flows, Eval harness supports warm-starting KV cache snapshots so comparisons are apples-to-apples. There was a slight glitch in the past where snapshots missed headers — should be fixed; we'll validate in the bench run.
10:40 Anya: Last thing — we'd like to export alerts to our PagerDuty and also to an internal CSV store.
10:47 Oliver: Both supported. Alert webhooks and scheduled CSV exports.
10:52 Maya: Ok wrapping up — recap and next steps. We'll send security pack, sample prompt set export, pilot pricing and a calendar invite for the bench run. Customer to pick 3 prompt sets and success metrics.
11:10 Tom: Thanks all. We'll review and aim to get prompt sets to you by Friday.
11:18 Priya: I'll review the security docs when you send them.
11:22 Maya: Great — talk soon.
11:25 (meeting ends)

Notes on transcript: Some auto-captions mislabeled names and technical terms (e.g., "KV cache" became "K-V cash" in parts). There are occasional filler words and cross talk. The timestamps are approximate every 30-90s.
